transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-11-02
Time: 14:00 PT
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Sofia (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Maya (Head of ML Ops, NorthArc), Jon (Platform Eng, NorthArc), Aisha (VP Product, NorthArc)
Shared links: 2027-11-02-northarc-deck-v2 (drive), benchmark-plan-draft (sheet), SOC2-brief.pdf

Summary:
Quick QBR/check-in focused on aligning on capacity and cost tradeoffs for NorthArc's fraud-detection rollout; agreed to run a targeted performance benchmark using customer's trace, clarified security/compliance asks (SOC2, KMS, SSO), and set next steps to share pricing for Dedicated vs Hosted pilot.

Topics:
- Current usage and projected ramp (500k -> 2M inference calls/mo over next 6 months)
- Cost drivers and batching/quantization opportunities
- Reliability SLOs and fallbacks (region routing, model variants)
- On‑prem/VPC constraints and audit logging
- Pilot definition and success criteria

Transcript:
[00:00] Sofia (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro — I'm Sofia, AE on the account, and with me is Liam, our systems SE. How's everyone?
[00:08] Maya (NorthArc): Hey, hi. Thanks, Sofia. We, uh, have Aisha and Jon on too. Appreciate you making time.
[00:12] Aisha (NorthArc): Hey all.
[00:14] Liam (Redwood SE): Morning/afternoon — I'll try to keep the deep perf bits concise but we'll share the bench plan after.
[00:18] Sofia: Goal for today: align on capacity needs and cost targets for the fraud model rollout, figure out what we need for a pilot — security questions first then perf. Sound right?
[00:26] Maya: Yeah, that sounds right. We're moving from a small POC to a full pilot and want to lock down expected spend and the reliability posture. Also procurement wants numbers.
[00:33] Jon: One correction — our traffic ramp is heavier than we said last time: current is about 500k inference calls per month but expected to double each month over three months for the initial product, so planning for ~2M by quarter end.
[00:45] Sofia: Great, helpful. Liam, do you want to take the perf/cost framing?
[00:48] Liam: Sure. So high level — cost per token isn't the only metric for you here since these are short single-turn inferences, it's per-request compute. We typically look at three levers to hit your numbers: batching, model quantization, and routing to cheaper model variants for low-risk decisions. For fraud detection I assume latency targets are tight — what's your p95 target?
[01:10] Maya: We want p95 under 120ms for online scoring. Higher for async. Right now our in-house infra sits around p95 180ms so that's one of the drivers to consider Redwood Dedicated.
[01:21] Liam: Understood. Dedicated gives more predictable p95 and capacity; hosted can be cheaper if you accept occasional tail variance and our smart routing. For example, with continuous batching and KV cache warm, we can push p95 down to ~90-110ms on the tuned model, but that depends on request pattern.
[01:38] Jon: What about cold cache spikes? When a new session or new user comes in, we see latency spike. Do you have graceful degradation or fallbacks?
[01:45] Liam: Yes — smart routing to smaller global variants, and automatic fallback policies. We can configure region fallback — so if your primary region is saturated we spill to another region or to a cheaper quantized model. We'll preserve correctness by adding confidence thresholds. There might be a small quality delta but for many fraud scorers that's acceptable for triage.
[02:05] Aisha: From product side, our main ask is: minimal false negatives, we can tolerate some false positives flagged for review but must keep latency tight. Also procurement flagged encryption at rest and KMS — they want to ensure key management.
[02:18] Sofia: We support customer-managed KMS in Private deployments and in Dedicated we have integrations with major KMS providers. For hosted, we offer envelope encryption with our managed keys but can set up a BYOK flow for enterprise. We'll attach the SOC2 and ISO evidence after this call.
[02:33] Maya: That's good. Also SSO and RBAC — some of our analysts need limited console access, not full model deploy.
[02:39] Sofia: We have SAML SSO and role-based access. You can map roles to route-level permissions. Liam, maybe quickly on observability?
[02:47] Liam: Console gives per-route cost and latency breakdown, token-level cost is less relevant here but per-request cost is shown. We also provide tracing hooks and audit logs with retention options. For security reviewers you can export audit logs to your SIEM via secure forwarders.
[03:02] Jon: Can those audit logs be stored in our VPC or do they flow through Redwood first?
[03:07] Liam: In Dedicated and Private we can push logs directly into your logging endpoint in the VPC. For hosted, logs are retained in Redwood's system but we can set up push. There are, uh — there are retention and egress considerations; we'll document that.
[03:21] Maya: Great. On cost — can you give a back-of-the-envelope for hosted vs dedicated for our projected 2M calls/month? We have target spend of <$10k/month to start, otherwise procurement won't sign off.
[03:33] Sofia: Rough numbers — depends on model size and token counts. For short requests we typically see the hosted price range X per 1k requests. (note: rough placeholders in transcript) For Dedicated, with reserved capacity, you get predictable throughput; your unit cost can drop by 30-50% depending on commitment and batchability. I will follow up with tailored pricing; Liam we'll need the sample trace.
[03:55] Liam: Yes, if you share anonymized request distribution and average token counts, we can simulate with our bin-packing and batching model and give you per-request cost estimates and latency distributions.
[04:06] Jon: We'll export that tonight. Also a procurement question: what's the minimum contract length for Dedicated?
[04:12] Sofia: Typically monthly reserved with discounts on annual commits. We can be flexible for pilots — often start with a 3-month pilot with a smaller commit and scale as you go.
[04:21] Aisha: About the pilot — can we run a short benchmark with our real model? We want to compare in-house p95 and error rates.
[04:30] Liam: Absolutely. Our standard benchmark plan is to run your model trace through hosted and Dedicated replicas; we capture p50/p95/p99, throughput, and quality regression. We'll run two configurations: quantized aggressive and a higher-precision baseline. We'll share the scripts.
[04:45] Maya: Any caveats about data residency when we run that bench? We cannot send raw PII.
[04:50] Liam: We'll use an anonymized or synthetic trace. Best practice is to replace identifiers with placeholders while preserving request length distribution and feature sparsity.
[04:58] Jon: Ok we'll prepare that.
[05:00] Sofia: On reliability, one of the concerns you raised earlier was graceful degradation — we can configure canaries and automatic fallback to a cached decision if the runtime can't respond within a threshold, so you avoid full failures. That would mean scoring returns a 'defer to manual review' or last-known-score.
[05:16] Aisha: That's acceptable as long as it's auditable and we can tune thresholds.
[05:20] Liam: Yep, thresholds are config. Also note that caching and KV usage helps hit latency — if you have sequential checks per user we can keep caches warm. But for highly random, low-reuse traffic the gains are less.
[05:33] Maya: In our synthetic trace many requests are first-touch so reuse is low. Can batching still help?
[05:38] Liam: It can — continuous batching can coalesce requests in micro-windows; latency impact is small if configured. We can run a simulation on your trace to show batching impact on p95 and cost.
[05:49] Jon: One more tough ask — our security team wants to validate auditability: full request/response hashes, who deployed what, and a tamper-evident log. Is that something you can provide?
[05:59] Sofia: Yes, we have immutable audit logs and signed deploy records in Dedicated/Private. For hosted we have similar logs but can provide export and attestations. We'll include samples in the SOC package.
[06:12] Maya: Okay that helps.
[06:14] Aisha: From go-to-market timeline, if the pilot looks good we want to start a staged rollout in January. Procurement needs numbers this month.
[06:22] Sofia: Sounds doable. Action items: we'll send pricing and SOC docs by Friday and Liam will send the bench plan.
[06:28] Liam: I'll also include the script and infrastructure instructions to run the perf, plus a small terraform snippet to replicate the environment in Dedicated.
[06:36] Jon: And we'll send you the anonymized trace tonight.
[06:40] Sofia: Awesome. Any other questions, concerns?
[06:43] Maya: Nothing major — just to confirm the pilot acceptance criteria: p95 <120ms, false negative rate not worse than current baseline, and monthly cost under your preliminary $10k target.
[06:55] Sofia: Yep that's captured. We'll write the pilot success criteria into the doc and send it across.
[06:59] Aisha: One last quick PS — do you have a runbook for incident response? Our ops team will want that.
[07:06] Liam: Yes, runbooks for Dedicated and Private are standard; for hosted we have an on-call SL and incident matrix. We'll attach samples.
[07:14] Sofia: Great. Okay let's recap then we can close.

Recap / Next steps called out verbally:
- Redwood to send pricing (hosted vs dedicated) and example SLA (Sofia)
- Redwood to share SOC2/ISO artifacts and sample audit log export (Sofia)

- Schedule pilot kickoff (target week of Nov 9)
